title: Plate up a canteen meal on a hand-held dinner plate: steak, hot dog, two wings and a bread roll, all inside the rim
instruction: Take the top plate off the stack and, holding it up the whole time, serve the steak, the hot dog, both chicken wings and the bread roll onto it from the pans with the serving tongs, no gripper touching the food and nothing sticking out past the plate's edge. Then deliver the served plate to the pick-up zone on the pass and let go.
context: Cafeteria cooks and servers dish up meals all day. O*NET lists 'Apportion and serve food to facility residents, employees, or patrons' for Cooks, Institution and Cafeteria (35-2012; 435,640 US workers, 137,290 in schools; BLS OEWS May 2023) and 'Select food items from serving or storage areas and place them in dishes, on serving trays, or in take-out bags' for Fast Food and Counter Workers (35-3023, titles include Cafeteria Server), 88,840 of them in schools and 141,760 in contract food service: over 660,000 together. On a staff-served line the server takes a plate, holds it by its edge or bottom (food-safety rule: 'HOLD plates by the bottom or at the very edge'), fills it from the pans and passes it over the counter. The difficulty is physical: a full plate of five portions covers about 64% of a 26 cm plate, so each must go where the next still fits inside the edge, without nudging the ones already there off the open rim, while the held plate takes the shifting load.
setup: A serving counter (the table) in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist (real trial: also a phone camera at counter height, with one tape mark 5 cm above the counter in its view). Positions in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y left of the midpoint between them; heights above the counter top. All objects true size. (1) Plates: a short stack of eight identical dinner plates, Carlisle Dallas Ware 4350002, white melamine, 10 1/4 in (26.0 cm) across, 2.15 cm tall (0.84 in, Boelter listing), 0.38 kg each (0.83 lb, Boelter listing), with a 3.2 cm rim (rim width and section estimated from product photos), stacked right side up and centred at x 30, y +10. The plates nest 1.2 cm apart, the foot of each on the floor of the one below (a Carlisle case of 48 is four stacks of 12 in a box 6.38 in tall, about 1.2 cm a plate), so the stack stands 10.6 cm and the top plate's rim sits 5 to 7 mm above the rim of the plate under it. The seven lower plates are one fixed body (2.7 kg of plates that do not shift under a hand); the top plate is free. (2) Two half-size stainless steam-table pans, Vollrath 30222 Super Pan V, 2 1/2 in deep (32.5 cm along x, 26.5 cm along y, 6.5 cm deep, 0.9 mm wall), fixed as if set in the line's wells: pan A centred x 38, y -30; pan B centred x 38, y -57. (3) In pan A, lying flat with their long axes along x: a steak with a fat edge along one side, 15 cm long, 7.1 cm wide at one end widening to 9.3 cm (8.2 cm on average), 2.2 cm thick, 270 g, centred x 38, y -24.5, and a hot dog in its bun with mustard (16 x 6 x 5 cm, 100 g) centred x 38, y -36. (4) In pan B: two whole chicken wings (drumette, flat and tip joined, 9.5 x 4.3 x 3 cm, 60 g each) at x 29, y -53 and x 29, y -64, long axes along x, drumette toward -x, and a round crusty bread roll (7.6 cm across, 5 cm tall, 45 g) at x 41, y -57. Real trial: food-safe display replicas, not cooked food, so nothing is wasted and no heat or grease reaches the grippers (food temperature plays no part in the act or the score): Life/form vinyl replicas, steak SKU 9283, hot dog in bun SKU 4634, hard roll SKU 9211 and the two wings printed in PETG from the task's own shapes, each brought to the mass above with steel shot sealed in a food-safe pouch under or inside it; weigh and measure each before the first trial and record it. Masses are cooked portions (estimates). Friction (estimates): food on melamine 0.4, food on food 0.5, plate on plate and on the pad 0.8. (5) Serving tongs: 12 in (30.5 cm) stainless spring utility tongs, Vollrath 4781230, 170 g, scalloped tips that spring 10.8 cm apart, lying closed side down on a folded cotton bar towel (35 x 12.6 x 0.8 cm, centred x 31, y -10), hinge at x 46, tips toward -x. All food is served with them: a gripper never touches the food. (6) Pick-up zone: a 35 x 35 x 1 cm stainless shelf pad centred x 38, y +44, just left of the plate stack, outlined on the counter by a 1.5 cm yellow tape line round it: the place on the pass where the guest collects the plate. It takes one plate, 4.5 cm to spare each way. Real trial: any flat 1 cm board of that size (about 15 USD) and floor-marking tape (about 5 USD). Real trial: clamp or tape the stack's bottom plate and both pans to the counter; before the first trial measure the pad's friction on melamine, the grip's pinch force, slip margin and the tongs' tip force, and record them. Nothing else is in reach.
scoring: Terms. Served with the tongs: no gripper (fingers, pads, palm, housing, wrist link) has touched the item (within 4 mm) at any time in the run; an item a gripper touched never counts. On the plate: the item is served with the tongs, rests on the plate or on food on it, no gripper touches it, the tongs have let it go, it moves under 0.2 m/s, and seen from straight above no part of it lies past the plate's outer edge; food that fell to the counter or the stack after leaving its pan never counts. Held clear: a gripper holds the plate, it rests on nothing else, and its lowest point is at least 5 cm above the counter. In the zone: seen from above the whole plate lies inside the yellow line, resting flat (tilt at most 6 degrees) on the pad. Score at the end of the run: 0.25, the plate is off the stack (held clear, or touching no part of the stack with its centre at least 26 cm from the stack's). 0.5, also all five items (steak, hot dog in bun, two wings, bread roll) are on the plate. 0.75, the plate is in the zone with all five on it, both grippers (fingers, palm, housing) and the tongs at least 8 mm from the plate and the food, and plate and food still (under 3 cm/s). 1.0, that state has held unbroken for the last 2 s. Void, score 0: food on the plate while the plate rests on anything (the stack, the counter, a pan's rim, the zone, food under it) before all five have been on it together held clear; or the plate let fall, held or not (any part of it going down faster than 0.45 m/s, a free fall from 1 cm). The 0.2 m/s, 4 mm, 8 mm, 3 cm/s and 0.45 m/s tests are simulation only; real trial: any visible contact between a gripper and the food in the wrist or counter video voids that item; real trial: a photo from straight above at the end, and overhead and counter-height video for rests, holds, gaps, stillness and drops.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz, GPU. Food is rigid simple solids at real portion sizes and cooked masses, one convex-hull collider each; friction is estimated. The tongs are a sprung hinge standing in for the real 12 in spring tongs, held by the gripper at one handle. The plate profile and the stack's 1.2 cm nesting pitch are estimates; the seven lower plates are one fixed body. The skill survives: the held plate takes five tong-served shapes inside its 26 cm edge and is set flat in a marked zone.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (4,000 steps, one valid session, final code); demo: 1.0 (step 3340, 167.0 s)
